title: The Glory Be
hook: the shortest Catholic prayer, praise to the three persons
carry: as it was in the beginning
tomorrow: The Apostles' Creed, line by line

segments.voice: Yesterday, knees and bows: to genuflect is to bend the knee. Your line was the body says it first.

Day one hundred. If you've come this far, you've kept at something for over three months, and that deserves a moment. So here's a fitting prayer for it, one that takes about seven seconds. It closes each decade of the rosary. It ends the psalms when monks and nuns and priests pray their daily hours. It fits in the gap between one task and the next. It asks for nothing. It confesses nothing. It just gives glory, and goes back to work.
screen: `ONE HUNDRED DAYS.` → `A SEVEN-SECOND PRAYER.` → `IT ASKS FOR NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Here it is, in its traditional English form: "Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen." Many Catholics today say Holy Spirit. In the old Latin: Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen. A prayer like this is a doxology, from two Greek words: doxa, glory, and logos, word. A glory-word. The Gloria at Mass is called the greater doxology, and this one the lesser. Look at its shape. The first line is the sign of the cross from day one, turned from a name into praise: Father, Son, Holy Spirit. The second line is all about time: past, present, future, in one breath. Some readers hear a history in that line. Christians once argued fiercely over whether the Son had always existed or had a beginning. Read that way, praying that the glory was the same in the beginning says, every day: he always was. An old argument, settled into rhythm. World without end is the old English way of saying forever; in the Latin, into the ages of ages. Catholics use the Glory Be like a period at the end of a sentence: after a psalm, after a decade, after a task. It closes things, and hands them back.
screen: `DOXA AND LOGOS: A GLORY-WORD.` · `FATHER, SON AND HOLY SPIRIT.` · `PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.` · `AN OLD ARGUMENT IN SEVEN SECONDS.` · then, large: `AS IT WAS IN THE BEGINNING, IS NOW, AND EVER SHALL BE.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you finished today, or will finish soon: a report, a load of laundry, a hard conversation. Picture stopping for seven seconds when it's done, before the next thing; if you pray, say the Glory Be over it, and if you don't, simply mark the end: done. Sit with the feeling of something finished.
Doxology. A glory-word: a short prayer of praise, like the Glory Be, to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Your line: as it was in the beginning. Is now, and ever shall be. One hundred days, and counting.
